text:
Jacob Fowler is 21, a week from his 22nd birthday, and Montreal's season is leaning on him. He has started 13 games, gone 9-2-2 with a .923 save percentage, and saved 12.4 goals more than his shots usually allow (goals saved above expected), 96th percentile among goalies. In his 20-game checkup, The Athletic's Arpon Basu framed it as Fowler giving the Canadiens time to figure things out.

The quality holds up under the hood. He's at .913 on medium-danger shots against a league .863, and .792 on the high-danger ones against .685, which is where goalies separate. Last season's 17 games came in at plus 6.0, so this isn't a hot month on an empty record, even if the book on him is still short.

The one flaw our numbers keep flagging is rebounds: 13.8% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds, against a league 10.8%. So far he has been stopping the second chance too. With Montreal coming off two straight losses, watch whether the defense in front of him starts clearing those pucks, because no goalie wins every scramble.
